bib.title: The Era of 1-bit LLMs: All Large Language Models are in 1.58 Bits

question: Can an LLM trained from scratch with ternary {-1,0,1} weights match FP16 Transformers in quality while cutting latency, memory, throughput and energy cost?
hypothesis: Ternary weights with explicit zero (feature filtering) give a stronger 1-bit model that matches full precision from 3B.
contributions: BitNet b1.58: ternary-weight 1-bit LLM variant with absmean quantization
Matches FP16 LLaMA from 3B in perplexity and end tasks
New scaling law/recipe and call for 1-bit hardware

method.summary: Transformer with nn.Linear replaced by BitLinear, trained from scratch with 1.58-bit weights (absmean quantization) and 8-bit activations, LLaMA-alike components. Compared to reproduced FP16 LLaMA at 700M-3.9B on 100B tokens, cost measured at up to 70B.
method.task: language model pretraining and zero-shot evaluation

datasets.name: ARC-e, ARC-c, HellaSwag, BoolQ, OpenbookQA, PIQA, Winogrande

models.name: BitNet b1.58
models.architecture: LLaMA-alike: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embedding, no biases; BitLinear

limits: No training hyperparameters, layer counts, optimizer, lr, hardware or compute stated: not reproducible from the paper
Quality shown only at 700M-3.9B; 700M and 1.3B are worse than FP16; 7B-70B only cost-measured, not trained for quality
Energy is a modelled arithmetic estimate, not measured
Speed measured with 2-bit kernel on GPU, not true ternary hardware
No code or weights released; KV cache 4-bit and MoE claims are future work
Comparison base is the authors' reproduced LLaMA; StableLM numbers copied from its report
